subject: science
intro: Natural selection is the main process driving evolution, and it results from four factors. First, populations have the potential to produce more offspring than can survive. Second, individuals have heritable genetic variation, so they differ in their traits. Third, resources like food and space are limited, so individuals compete to survive. Fourth, individuals with traits better suited to the environment tend to survive and reproduce more, passing those traits on. Over generations, the helpful traits become more common in the population.

items.prompt: Name the four factors that drive natural selection.

steps: Natural selection comes from how populations and traits interact.
Populations can produce more offspring than survive, and individuals have heritable variation.
Resources are limited so individuals compete, and better-suited individuals reproduce more, so those are the four factors.
solution.answer: Overproduction of offspring, heritable variation, competition for limited resources, and increased reproduction of better-suited individuals.

items.prompt: In a population of beetles, some are better camouflaged than others. Explain how natural selection could make camouflage more common over generations.

steps: The beetles vary in camouflage, a heritable trait, and more are born than can survive.
Predators and limited resources mean beetles compete to survive.
Better-camouflaged beetles survive and reproduce more, passing on camouflage, so it becomes more common over generations.
solution.answer: Better-camouflaged beetles survive and reproduce more, passing on camouflage, so it becomes more common over generations.

items.prompt: Why is heritable variation necessary for natural selection?

steps: Natural selection acts on differences among individuals.
If there were no heritable variation, all individuals would be the same and none would have an advantage to pass on.
So heritable variation is necessary because it provides the differences that selection can act on and pass to offspring.
solution.answer: Because selection needs heritable differences among individuals to act on and pass to offspring; without variation there is nothing to select.

items.prompt: Why do individuals in a population compete?

steps: Populations tend to produce more offspring than the environment can support.
Resources like food and space are limited.
So individuals compete for the limited resources.
solution.answer: Because resources are limited and more offspring are produced than can survive, so individuals compete for resources.

items.prompt: A faster rabbit escapes predators better than a slower one. Explain how this leads to more fast rabbits over time.

steps: Speed is a heritable trait that varies among the rabbits.
Faster rabbits survive predators better and reproduce more.
They pass on the fast trait, so over generations fast rabbits become more common.
solution.answer: Faster rabbits survive and reproduce more, passing on their speed, so fast rabbits become more common over generations.

items.prompt: Construct an explanation for how a population of bacteria can become resistant to an antibiotic through natural selection.

steps: The bacteria vary, and a few happen to have a heritable trait that resists the antibiotic.
The antibiotic is a limited-survival pressure that kills non-resistant bacteria, leaving the resistant ones.
The resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, passing on resistance, so over generations the population becomes resistant.
solution.answer: A few bacteria vary with resistance; the antibiotic kills the rest, so the resistant ones survive and reproduce, making the population resistant over generations.
